idiom_name: domain interface + one implementation that owns the messaging client, the correlation table and the error mapping
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: declare an interface in domain terms (placeOrder(Order): OrderId, checkStock(sku): Stock) and implement it once per external system. The implementation owns everything the caller must not know: payload assembly and serialization, the reply address (a private inbox, callback queue or reply channel), the correlation id, a bounded table of pending calls, the per-call timeout and the translation of broker faults, timeouts and fault messages into a small domain error set. When the stack offers a gateway framework (a generated proxy for an annotated interface, an injected request client, a job class with an enqueue method), prefer that over hand-writing this component - the structure is the same, only the plumbing is provided. Keep the contract coarse-grained: one method per message, not a mirror of the remote object's accessors.
code_sketch:
interface InventoryGateway:                    # domain-facing contract
    check_stock(sku: String) -> Stock          # typed, no messaging types

class AmqpInventoryGateway(InventoryGateway):  # owns transport + correlation
    def check_stock(self, sku):
        id, slot = self.new_pending_call()     # correlation id + pending entry
        self.publish(target, payload=sku, reply_to=inbox, correlation_id=id)
        return self.await_reply(slot, timeout=5s)   # fault/timeout -> domain error
pitfalls: Letting the interface expose messaging types (message objects, headers, correlation ids) recreates the coupling the pattern removes.
A gateway instance shared across threads or coroutines usually is not safe: connection, channel and pending-call state need explicit synchronization or per-caller instances.
Skipping the timeout turns 'broker is down' into 'threads are exhausted'; skipping idempotency makes every caller-side retry a possible duplicate execution.

Wrong move: model a remote gateway like an in-process object with one method per field -> fine-grained round trips multiply latency and failure windows -> instead expose coarse-grained use-case methods with request DTOs.

Wrong move: retry every timeout blindly -> a reply may arrive after the remote operation already ran, so retries duplicate side effects -> instead use idempotency keys and classify the outcome as unknown.

Wrong move: keep an unbounded pending-call table -> abandoned callers and late replies retain correlation state until memory pressure -> instead bound and expire entries and discard unknown or duplicate replies.
